name: Dr. Meera Patel (Sociolinguistics)
note: When family members reconcile after conflict or long absence, honorific shifts from casual 'toran' to 'toran-ya' or 'toran-ma'. Avoid 'koba' entirely; it conveys contempt or disowning. S014 represents a reconciliation moment.

name: Prof. Julian Vance (Typology)
topic: Syntactic SOV Constraints and Lexicon Authenticity
note: SOV word order is structurally fixed for declarative clauses. Any SVO instance in vendor drafts represents translation leakage from English. Also, 'baxu' in Dictionary A is a ghost word or fabricated trap; 'dara' is supported by all 5 oral interviews.

name: Elder Kavi Nair (Community Consultant)
note: Viewers hated 'swagatam' in the pilot—it sounded like a formal state broadcast. Native speakers say 'aayo-re'. For negation, young people sometimes say 'nira' before the verb, but elders always prefix 'ni-' onto the verb stem.
